dimensions.label: Value innovation
dimensions.description: Does the company simultaneously drive down costs AND lift buyer value? Core Blue Ocean move — pursuing both usually creates uncontested space.

dimensions.label: Uncontested market space
dimensions.description: Is the company competing in a red ocean (crowded, price-driven) or a genuinely new/uncontested space where the rules aren't set yet?

dimensions.label: New demand creation
dimensions.description: Does the company convert non-customers into customers, or is it fighting for share within an existing pie?

dimensions.label: Distinctive strategic move
dimensions.description: Is there one identifiable big strategic move (product, model, geography) that defines the moat, or is the story incremental?

dimensions.label: Cost + value alignment
dimensions.description: Have they broken the value-cost trade-off through elimination / reduction / raising / creation of value elements?

dimensions.rationale: Custom ASIC co-design reportedly delivers up to 30% better power efficiency and 40% higher inference throughput than merchant GPUs (per industry analysis), while Broadcom's own GAAP operating margin still expanded to 48.9% this quarter.

Broadcom reportedly holds ~60-70% share of the custom AI ASIC design market (per industry research), a narrower and less-contested niche than merchant-GPU sales, though Marvell competes directly for the same hyperscaler design wins.

AI semiconductor revenue grew 143% y/y to $10.8B this quarter and management guided next-quarter AI semiconductor growth above 200% y/y (company-disclosed) — hyperscalers that previously bought only merchant GPUs are commissioning custom silicon.

Broadcom's multi-generation XPU co-design partnerships (seven TPU generations with Google since 2014, per industry reporting) plus a reported ~90% share of data-center switching silicon pair two moats hyperscalers can't easily disintermediate.
GAAP operating margin expanded 9.5ppt y/y to 48.9% this quarter, which the CFO attributed directly to operating leverage from scaling AI-driven revenue against a slower-growing cost base.

screens.verdict: Custom AI-ASIC co-design (AI semiconductor revenue +143% y/y to $10.8B, operating margin up 9.5ppt to 48.9%) pairs a narrower, less-contested niche than merchant GPUs with genuine cost/value alignment — the strongest composite in this batch.

sources.ref: Tom's Hardware: The custom AI ASIC state of play (May 2026)

dimensions.rationale: Google Cloud grew 82% y/y to $24.8B this quarter, aided by newly-started TPU-system revenue recognition — custom silicon lets Alphabet offer an AI-compute alternative to GPU pricing while still meeting workload performance needs.

Selling TPU systems directly (started this quarter) is a newer commercial category than reselling third-party GPUs, though Alphabet still competes head-on with AWS, Azure and Nvidia for the same AI-infrastructure spend.

Alphabet and Meta are reportedly in advanced discussions for Meta to lease Google TPUs starting in 2026 (per industry reporting) — converting a rival's AI-infrastructure spend that would otherwise go to Nvidia into Google Cloud demand.

Google Cloud began recognizing TPU-system sales revenue this quarter for the first time, a milestone the company's own filing credits as a driver of Cloud's 82% y/y growth — a distinctive vertically-integrated silicon strategy versus reselling merchant GPUs.

Google Cloud revenue growth of 82% y/y this quarter suggests improving unit economics from owning the TPU stack, though the company does not disclose a Cloud-segment margin figure this quarter to confirm the cost side directly.

screens.verdict: Vertically-integrated TPU silicon began generating direct systems-sale revenue this quarter, contributing to Cloud's 82% y/y growth to $24.8B — a distinctive infrastructure bet still competing head-on with AWS, Azure and Nvidia rather than in uncontested space.

sources.ref: Constellation Research: Google Cloud starts shipping TPU systems

dimensions.rationale: Gross margin hit 50.1% this quarter (including ~2pt of tariff-refund benefit) alongside double-digit y/y growth across iPhone, Mac and Services — value keeps compounding but pricing stays premium, not cost-down.
The premium smartphone and services market remains highly contested against Samsung, Google and Chinese OEMs — not a genuinely new or under-competed space.
Services growth largely converts Apple's own existing 1.15B-plus device install base (per industry research) into subscription revenue rather than creating a wholly new customer pool.

The company's own release called this its 'strongest June quarter ever' with double-digit growth across iPhone, Mac and Services and every geographic segment — Services layering a structurally different, higher-margin revenue stream onto the hardware base.

Gross margin of 50.1% and diluted EPS growth of 28.7% y/y show real value-cost alignment this quarter, though ~2pt of the margin and $0.11 of the EPS gain are a one-time tariff-refund tailwind the filing itself discloses.

screens.verdict: Hardware-plus-services flywheel posting record margins (50.1% gross margin, including a ~2pt tariff-refund tailwind) inside a mature, contested premium-device market — a moderate composite reflecting real differentiation without a genuinely new market.

sources.ref: TechLila: The Apple Ecosystem Lock-In Statistics 2026

dimensions.rationale: Microsoft 365 Copilot reached over 30 million paid seats (company-disclosed) while Azure grew 43% y/y — embedded AI raises per-seat value even as cloud scale keeps compute unit costs falling.
Enterprise cloud and AI are intensely contested against AWS, Google Cloud and Oracle — Azure competes head-on rather than in uncontested territory.

Microsoft 365 Copilot's 30M+ paid seats (company-disclosed) represent net-new AI-feature spend layered onto an existing installed base, converting existing seats into incremental ARPU rather than pure non-customer conversion.

CEO Nadella cited Azure revenue surpassing $100B for the fiscal year alongside Copilot's 30M+ paid-seat milestone as the company's core AI-platform thesis — one identifiable integrated distribution play across Windows, Microsoft 365 and Azure.

Azure's 43% y/y growth suggests scale leverage, but cash and short-term investments fell to $76.8B from $94.6B y/y as capex absorbed $35.8B this quarter — the near-term cost side of the trade-off remains unresolved.

screens.verdict: Azure (+43% y/y) and Copilot's 30M+ paid seats extend an AI-embedded platform strategy across a highly contested enterprise-cloud market, with a heavy capex ramp keeping the cost side of the value-cost trade-off unresolved this quarter.

sources.ref: Directions on Microsoft: Microsoft's AI Strategy

dimensions.rationale: Gross margin rebounded to 74.9% from 60.5% y/y while Data Center revenue grew 92% y/y to $75.2B — buyer performance keeps rising but NVIDIA captures most of the surplus via premium pricing, not a cost-down transfer.
NVIDIA holds ~80% AI GPU share per industry research, but the space is hyper-contested: AMD, Broadcom-built custom ASICs, and Google's TPU 8t/8i all compete for the same AI-infrastructure spend.
Data Center revenue +92% y/y to $75.2B reflects new AI-infrastructure buyers (cloud, sovereign, enterprise) entering compute markets that didn't exist at this scale a few years ago.

CUDA's software ecosystem (4M+ developers per industry research) locks frameworks like PyTorch/TensorFlow to NVIDIA hardware — one identifiable moat, though ROCm 7 and Triton are reported to be narrowing the gap in some workloads.
NVIDIA competes on premium performance, not cost — gross margin near 75% shows pricing power captured internally rather than a broken value-cost trade-off passed to buyers.

screens.verdict: Dominant AI-compute supplier (Data Center revenue +92% y/y to $75.2B) with a real CUDA-ecosystem moat, but competing in a hyper-contested space against ASIC and inference-focused alternatives rather than uncontested territory.

sources.ref: Alphastreet: Nvidia's CUDA Lock-In and Supply Scarcity

dimensions.rationale: AWS operating margin expanded to 39.4% from 32.9% y/y even while scaling AI workloads — the company is capturing cost efficiency gains from custom Trainium silicon (per industry reporting) rather than passing them fully to price.
Cloud infrastructure, retail and advertising are all highly contested against Azure, Google Cloud, Walmart and Google/Meta ads — not uncontested space.
AWS's fastest growth in 18 quarters (+37% y/y to $42.2B, company-disclosed) reflects capturing incremental AI-workload demand more than creating a wholly new category.

AWS's Project Rainier custom-silicon buildout (per industry reporting) plus a combined $100B+ of 2025-2026 capex is a single distinctive infrastructure bet layered onto the existing retail-logistics-cloud-ads flywheel.
TTM free cash flow swung to a $7.6B outflow from an $18.2B inflow as capex rose $66.1B y/y (company-disclosed) — the cost side of the ledger is currently negative even as AWS operating income grows.

screens.verdict: AWS posted its fastest growth in 18 quarters (+37% y/y, margin up to 39.4%) while TTM free cash flow swung negative on a $66.1B y/y capex rise — real operating leverage offset by a currently negative cost/value trade-off in AI infrastructure spend.

sources.ref: VaaSBlock: AWS Amazon AI Competitive Position 2026

dimensions.rationale: Ad price per impression rose 12% y/y even as impressions grew 14% y/y (both company-disclosed), and Reality Labs posted a $4.62B quarterly operating loss with no near-term buyer-value payoff — mixed evidence against a clean value-innovation read.
The core advertising business competes directly with Google, Amazon and TikTok for the same advertiser budgets — not uncontested space.

Llama's open-weights distribution (Llama 5 shipped April 2026 per industry reporting) aims to make Meta's model layer the default developer substrate, a demand-creation play distinct from the core ad auction.

Meta split its AI strategy in April 2026, shipping Llama 5 as open-weights alongside a closed Muse Spark model (per industry reporting) — a distinctive bet to commoditize the model layer while ring-fencing its ad-targeting edge.

Total costs and expenses rose 55% y/y on $2.40B of legal-proceedings charges and $1.18B of severance (company-disclosed), compressing operating margin from 43% to 31% this quarter — a clear cost/value deterioration, not alignment.

screens.verdict: Core ad business grew 28% y/y but operating margin compressed 12ppt on legal and severance charges, while a dual-track open/closed Llama strategy targets AI-adjacent demand creation — a contested core market weighs down a distinctive model-layer bet.
